title: Two groups created at once were handed the same tap prefix
foundBy: session agent, chasing a campaign smoke tier that failed whenever two scenarios ran at once, 2026-09-08

evidence.verified: Two cs-sandbox creates in two new groups, launched together. Before: p1 rc=0 in 6s, p2 rc=1 in 137s on 'microVM failed to become ready within 2m0s'. After: p1 rc=0 in 6s, p2 rc=0 in 7s, with each group's tap on a prefix of its own rather than one prefix for both. TestConcurrentGroupsGetDistinctTapPrefixes fails without the lock and passes with it.

resolution: ensureGroup now reserves through reserveGroup, which takes the host-wide create lock around the load-or-mint of the group record: the tap prefix, and the write that records it. The record goes in under that lock and the artifacts are made outside it, which reverses the old order. It has to be that way round, because the record IS the reservation: a create that provisioned first and recorded second would hold nothing meanwhile. Wrapping the whole of ensureGroup was tried first and deadlocks. EnsureNetwork takes the same file lock, and reentrancy there is per Lock value rather than per process.
details:
allocTapPrefix answers by reading which prefixes the recorded groups already hold, and it ran with no lock. Two creates for two NEW groups, started at the same moment, both read that pool before either had written to it. Both then took the lowest free answer.

What that costs is not a duplicate name in a file. A VM tap is named from its group's prefix plus its address's last octet, and both groups allocate from .200 up, so both VMs derived the same interface name. TapUp is idempotent by name: the second one found the first group's tap already present, skipped creating it, and re-mastered it onto its own bridge. That left the robbed microVM with no route off any bridge at all.

The failure then surfaced 120 seconds later, as the robbed create timing out on FC-VM-READY, naming a serial log that showed the guest booting normally. Nothing in that message points at group creation, which is why this took a bisection between two sandbox versions to find rather than a reading of the error.

It was never possible to create two groups at once. The previous release failed the same test immediately instead, with 'rootlessport listen tcp 127.0.0.1:2400: bind: address already in use' from two gateways racing for one published port. Making the gateway port opt-in removed that collision and left this one, which is quieter and slower.

Found from cs-campaign, whose smoke tier is one campaign per scenario and one group per campaign. Running its six scenarios in parallel failed two of them at a time, always on a two-minute readiness bound. The host was sitting at load 0.5 with 38 GiB free, so nothing about it was short.
